object_description: six small buildings of different design forming a quarter around a system of public squares
design_condition: the programme is divided into small units subordinated to a system of public spaces, creating a veritable small quarter at the interface between three different types of city

positive: The decision to divide the programme into small units subject to a system of public spaces is courageous
It offers remarkable advantages for the urban location
A veritable small quarter is created at the interface between three different types of city
It serves as an urban communication element thanks to intelligent geometry and extreme finesse
The small corner square forms a hinge between the old town and the campus complex
It is at the same time an appropriate centre of the new university town
The second space at the end of the staircase is just as well placed and modestly sized
Together with the transverse alleys they add high-quality public urban open spaces
The tree plantings form a soft transition to the hillside
The auditorium building is effectively positioned in the most prominent location on the new square
The two restaurants on the ground floors of the neighbouring buildings are just as obvious
The fragmentation creates well-lit and pleasantly manageable rooms
The small city within the city presents itself uniformly with finely nuanced variations
This ensures it the necessary presence
The robust, unpretentious outward-turned support system suggests practicality
The fusion with the city and its spaces expresses the open and urban attitude of the university
negative: The degree of sealing is naturally high and the northern parking requires a retaining wall
Roof areas heavily occupied by photovoltaics conflict with extensive green roofs
The division into six different buildings is anything but unproblematic
The organisation of the research and teaching floors is inadequately defined
The stated goal of flexibility and adaptability is hardly given architectural form
The fragmentation creates a lot of circulation space, costs and energy losses
Operational processes and flexibility are severely limited by the split across several buildings
Dividing departments into different buildings risks isolating them from one another
It requires the willingness to walk across the street to interact with colleagues
Possible obstacles, not least weather-related, cannot be ignored
The connecting basement solves logistics but not interpersonal communication
The support system is not without structural and building physics challenges
